title: From Small to Large: Assessing Medical Reasoning, Benchmark Contamination, and Model Size in Language Models
reasons: 医学、生物医学或临床专题，超出当前 Agent 与通用模型评测方向
missingSignals: 明确提出新的评测资料或框架

evidence.label: 描述任务、问题或评测环境
evidence.excerpt: Large language models (LLMs) now answer medical exam questions at or above expert level, but it is unclear whether such scores reflect clinical competence, or are instead affected by the format of the questions being asked (e.g., multiple-choice versus open-ended), prior exposure to the benchmarks, and the difficulty of the questions.

evidence.label: 描述评分指标或评测协议
evidence.excerpt: Withholding the answer choices, however, makes every model struggle: mean accuracy falls from 82.3% to 50.9%, and the two largest drops belong to the medically specialised models.

evidence.label: 报告基线或多个模型的评测
evidence.excerpt: In the standard multiple-choice setting, the strongest models exceed the human-expert baseline on MedQA-USMLE and PubMedQA, but the smaller models trail their larger models by 8.7 percentage points and only two of the six pass the human-expert bar on the licensing examination.

evidence.label: 给出任务规模或覆盖范围
evidence.excerpt: In this study, we evaluate fourteen current models from six leading providers, one smaller and one larger model from each provider with two additional open-weight models, on 3,076 questions from four medical benchmarks (MedQA-USMLE, MedMCQA, PubMedQA, and MedBullets) under standard multiple choice, the same questions with the answer choices withheld, and reconstruction of a hidden question from its choices alone.
